result.summary: The street features narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks directly adjacent to the roadway without a buffer or street trees. While traffic volume appears low, the lack of pedestrian-oriented infrastructure like marked crossings or traffic calming measures reduces overall safety.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalks
hazards.description: The sidewalks on both sides of the street are very narrow, providing little space for pedestrians to pass each other or maintain distance from traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no planting strip or furniture zone separating the narrow walkway from the travel lane, exposing pedestrians to moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the sidewalk adjacent to the roadway

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is uneven and shows signs of cracking and wear, creating potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk area on the left and right foreground

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the width of the sidewalks to meet accessibility standards and provide a more comfortable walking environment.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install a buffer zone with trees or vegetation between the sidewalk and the curb to protect pedestrians and improve the streetscape.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the nearest intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk that is currently in fair condition with visible weed growth. The environment lacks traffic calming measures, lane markings, and a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, creating a basic but unprotected pedestrian space.

hazards.name: Sidewalk degradation
hazards.description: Weeds and cracks in the sidewalk surface create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground along the sidewalk edge.

hazards.name: Blind corner at alleyway
hazards.description: The tall fences on either side of the narrow alleyway create a blind spot for pedestrians and any vehicles or cyclists emerging from the gap.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image where the gap between the white and brown fences is located.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair cracks and remove vegetation to ensure a smooth, hazard-free walking surface.

interventions.title: Roadway Markings
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to better define the travel lanes and organize vehicle movement.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Alleyway
interventions.description: Ensure the area immediately adjacent to the alleyway entrance is kept clear of obstructions to improve sightlines between pedestrians and emerging traffic.

result.summary: The street features narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane residential roadway. Pedestrians lack physical separation from vehicle traffic, and the walkway on the left is further constrained by utility pole obstructions.

hazards.name: Degraded Walkway Surface
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image is severely cracked and overgrown with weeds, creating significant tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and midground

hazards.name: Fixed Object Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow left-side sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to step into the roadway or against building walls.
hazards.location_in_image: Left sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no horizontal separation or buffer between the narrow walking path and the travel lane for vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction and Widening
interventions.description: Repair the degraded sidewalk surfaces and widen the walkways to meet ADA standards, ensuring a clear path of travel.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Move utility poles to a dedicated furniture zone or underground the lines to remove obstructions from the pedestrian clear zone.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or chicanes to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context where sidewalks are narrow.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide paved apron serving as a walkway and driveway access for residential garages, lacking any physical separation or curbing from the narrow roadway. The presence of overgrown vegetation and utility poles further obstructs the path, creating an informal space that prioritizes vehicle access over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Lack of vertical separation
hazards.description: The absence of a curb or barrier between the roadway and the pedestrian walkway allows vehicles to easily encroach on the walking space.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edge where the asphalt road meets the concrete apron.

hazards.name: Walkway obstruction
hazards.description: Overgrown vegetation and a utility pole narrow the usable path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, around the wooden utility pole.

hazards.name: Continuous driveway conflict zone
hazards.description: The entire frontage serves as vehicle access for garages, creating multiple points of potential conflict with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire foreground and mid-ground paved area.

interventions.title: Install Raised Curbing
interventions.description: Construct a raised curb to physically separate the pedestrian walkway from the travel lane, preventing vehicle encroachment.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Regularly clear overgrown weeds and maintain the walkway to ensure a clear, unobstructed path for all users.

interventions.title: Delineated Pedestrian Path
interventions.description: Use pavement markings or contrasting materials to clearly define a dedicated pedestrian zone separate from the garage access areas.
